replies.question: 2. Draw the pattern of the electric field around: a) a positive charge b) a negative charge. Explain what the arrows mean and explain at which points the strength of the field is greatest.
replies.reply:
**Around a positive charge the lines point straight outward, away from it; around a negative charge they point straight inward, toward it.** Both patterns are radial and look identical apart from which way the arrows face.

```
      (a) positive                  (b) negative
          \  |  /                       \  |  /
           \ | /                         \ | /
        ---- ( + ) ----               ---- ( - ) ----
           / | \                         / | \
          /  |  \                       /  |  \
```

**What the arrows mean** — an arrow shows the direction of the force that the field would exert on a small **positive test charge** placed at that point. So it points away from a positive charge (repulsion) and toward a negative charge (attraction). A negative charge would simply feel the force the opposite way.

**Where the field is strongest** — at the points **closest to the charge**, where the lines are packed most densely together. The field weakens as you move away, because the lines spread farther apart. You can see this in the diagram: the lines are crowded near the centre and thin out at the edges.

replies.question: 3. Repeat question 2 for the electric field: a) around a positive and a negative charge b) around two negative charges c) between two oppositely charged flat metal plates.
replies.reply:
# Electric field patterns

**(a) Single charges** — lines point **outward from a positive charge** and **inward to a negative charge**, both straight and radial.

```
   ( + )              ( - )
  ->  ^  <-         <-  |  ->
 <--  +  -->        -->  -  <--
  ->  v  <-         <-  |  ->
```

**(b) Two negative charges** — the lines curve away from each other and bend outward, leaving a **gap in the middle** where the two fields cancel. The lines repel, so no line joins the two charges.

```
      <--  |  -->    <--  |  -->
         \ | /          \ | /
        <- ( - )  X  ( - ) ->
```

**(c) Two oppositely charged flat plates** — the field is **uniform**: straight parallel lines of equal spacing, running from the positive plate to the negative plate, same strength everywhere between them.

```
 + + + + + + + + +
  |   |   |   |
  |   |   |   |
  |   |   |   |
 - - - - - - - - -
```

**Arrows** show the force on a small positive test charge: away from positive, toward negative.

**Greatest strength** where the lines are **closest together** — nearest the charges in (a) and (b), and in (c) the field is the same at every point between the plates.
